entities.summary: Gaius Oppius Sabinus was a Roman Senator who held at least one office in the emperor's service. Born into a plebeian family, he rose to prominence through his intelligence and loyalty. He was ordinary consul in the year 84 CE, serving as the colleague of emperor Domitian. This appointment was part of Domitian's efforts to centralize power and maintain control over the Roman Senate. As consul, Sabinus would have played a role in the administration of justice, governance, and military affairs. His involvement in the imperial administration reflects the complex web of relationships between the emperor, the Senate, and the Roman people. Despite his moderate reputation, Sabinus's career was shaped by the tumultuous politics of the Late Empire. The legacy of his tenure as consul remains a testament to the enduring impact of the Roman imperial system on Western politics and governance. The 2017 excavation of his tomb in Rome uncovered a richly decorated inscribed altar, which now stands as a poignant reminder of the lives and legacies of Rome's lesser-known citizens. As a symbol of the senator's family, the altar serves as a poignant artifact of the Roman people's cultural heritage.
